desc:
A convex polygon has m labelled vertices. A triangulation splits it into triangles by drawing diagonals that do not cross each other. Return the number of different triangulations, modulo 1,000,000,007. Two triangulations are different when they use different sets of diagonals.

m = 3 -> 1   (a triangle is already triangulated)
m = 4 -> 2
m = 5 -> 5
hints: Pick the side between vertices 0 and m - 1. In any triangulation it belongs to exactly one triangle, whose third vertex is some vertex k.
That split leaves two smaller convex polygons, one on the vertices 0..k and one on k..m - 1, that are triangulated independently. So T(m) = sum of T(a) * T(b) over the splits.
The recurrence is the Catalan recurrence. The answer is the Catalan number C<sub>m - 2</sub>, which equals C(2n, n) / (n + 1) with n = m - 2.
editorial: Let T(j) count triangulations of a polygon with j vertices. Fix the side (0, m - 1). Its triangle has apex k for some 0 < k < m - 1, and the two remaining regions are polygons with k + 1 and m - k vertices. Summing over k gives the convolution recurrence of the Catalan numbers.
Solving the recurrence gives T(m) = Cm-2 = (2n)! / (n! (n + 1)!) with n = m - 2. Computing it modulo the prime needs factorials up to 2n and two modular inverses, so the work is linear in m.
Small values for a check: m = 3 gives C<sub>1</sub> = 1, m = 4 gives C<sub>2</sub> = 2 and m = 6 gives C<sub>4</sub> = 14.
solution:
def countTriangulations(m):
    MOD = 10 ** 9 + 7
    n = m - 2
    fact = [1] * (2 * n + 2)
    for i in range(1, 2 * n + 2):
        fact[i] = fact[i - 1] * i % MOD
    cat = fact[2 * n] * pow(fact[n], MOD - 2, MOD) % MOD * pow(fact[n + 1], MOD - 2, MOD) % MOD
    return cat
